On April 19, 1995, the worst act of domestic terrorism in our nation’s history took place at the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. Today marked thirty-one years since that tragic and miserable day. However, even though the time has passed, as Oklahomans, the Oklahoma City bombing will forever be imprinted in our minds and hearts.
 
Today, we first remember and grieve the 168 innocent lives that were cut short on that dark day. I will never forget the heartbreak, grief, and distress I felt as I witnessed mothers, fathers, children, and friends watch their loved ones be brutally taken from them.
 
I will also never forget the way Oklahoma responded to such a tragedy. After being rattled and thrown onto the world stage without any warning, we could have panicked. Yet, we didn’t. Instead, our state responded strongly, quickly, and empathetically. To this day, I can truly say this is one of the many reasons I am proud to be an Oklahoman.
 
So, on the 31st anniversary of the Oklahoma City Bombing, let us take the time to mourn the lives that were prematurely taken, grieve with those who lost a loved one that day, and thank our first responders and governing officials who responded with courage. We must ensure they are not forgotten.

We also brought them in to speak directly with my colleagues Chairman Mark Amodei, Joaquin Castro, Juan Ciscomani, and Adriano Espaillat so they could share those concerns firsthand and make clear that what impacts one community affects others. Furthermore, they met with staff from the Appropriations Committee to discuss apprenticeship programs.

During their previous trip to Washington, D.C., I was able to connect the South Texas Builders with senior ICE leadership to address enforcement operations targeting worksites. Those conversations delivered results. ICE has shifted its focus away from worksites and toward individuals with criminal records, instead of those who have lived here for years and contributed to our communities.

That shift has made a real difference. It helps keep crews on the job, projects moving, and housing supply from falling further behind demand.

This is the kind of work that matters: bringing people together, cutting through the noise, and getting results that show up back home.

I’m grateful for the partnership with the South Texas Builders Association, and I’ll keep working to move practical, bipartisan solutions that support our workforce and keep South Texas growing.

When I first ran for State Representative back in 1992, my aspiration was to represent my hometown of Tarkio, Missouri. I was a twenty-seven year old farmer who just wanted to stand up for a way of life and his community.  I never could have imagined where that decision would take me.   

For 8 years in the Missouri House and Senate, I fought for Northwest Missourians. From deregulating vehicle inspections, to standing for chain gangs, to securing funding for rural schools in the desegregation fight, I never lost sight of why I was sent to Jefferson City. Then, in 2000, the good, hardworking people of Missouri’s Sixth District entrusted me to be their voice in Congress.    

For 26 years, I have had the privilege of serving, culminating in becoming the Chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and passing some of the most significant legislation in our nation’s history.  The responsibility entrusted to me is not something I have ever taken for granted. Not for a single day.   

What I’m most proud of is the work my team did when Washington made life harder for the people of Missouri’s Sixth. Together, we stood with hundreds of thousands of Missourians in their toughest moments.  We helped them cut through red tape and navigate a system that often felt stacked against them.  We got them answers and fought to deliver real results when they needed them most.   

I’ve said all of that to say this: After considerable reflection, 2026 will be my final year in Congress.  This wasn’t an easy decision, but it’s the right one. I believe in making room for the next generation. It’s time to pass the torch and allow a new guard of conservative leaders to step forward and chart a path forward for Missourians.    

That doesn’t mean I’m slowing down, not even close.  As I enter the 4th quarter of my life, I have more left in me. As many of you know, I don't let grass grow under my feet. We’ve still got a lot of work to do. I’m going to fight to protect Missouri interests as we work to shape this year’s Highway Bill. I plan to finish this last term the same way I started, full speed ahead.   

Maintaining our strong democratic republic will always depend on good people stepping up to serve from every corner of our great nation. I’m grateful for my colleagues in both parties, for the people I’ve worked alongside, and even for the opponents who challenged me and made me better. Public service isn’t easy. It takes hard work, humility, a thick skin, and a willingness to fight for what’s right.   

At the end of the day, I’m still the farmer from Northwest Missouri. You’ll find me back home on the farm nearly every weekend, after all, it is planting season. In fact, I’ll probably be on a tractor this weekend. And come Monday, I’ll be heading back through Kansas City on my way to D.C. to keep doing the job you sent me there to do.   From the bottom of my heart, thank you.    

It has been the honor of a lifetime.

RT by @RepHankJohnson: I fully condemn the hateful rhetoric, lies, cruel and deliberate misinformation, and threats that my family, my staff, and I have been subjected to since the Iran War began nearly 8 weeks ago. These coordinated attacks and threats have only continued to worsen, most recently after I introduced Articles of Impeachment against Pete Hegseth. This conduct has crossed the line into threats to our physical safety, which we have reported to law enforcement.

Bad actors have tried to smear my family and staff by circulating fake and AI-generated images and flat-out lying that my parents and I are not U.S. citizens. They have pushed xenophobic and sexist attacks and amplified absurd conspiracy theories about my family. They’ve even gone so far as to spread the outright lie that I am somehow tied to the regime. I will say this once and move on: these absurd allegations are entirely false and I denounce them in the strongest terms.

These attacks aren’t about truth; they’re the product of desperation from those trying to distract from a failing, illegal war, rising costs of living, and an administration with no coherent strategy while Americans pay the price at the pump. And while they spread lies, American service members are being put in harm’s way, with real casualties mounting in a war that lacks both justification and direction.

Let me reiterate, once again, that I have been unequivocal in my opposition to the brutal Islamic Republic regime, its repression of women, and its support for terrorism. My record on this issue is longstanding and crystal clear. My family has personally experienced the regime’s brutality. 

It is in part why I am who I am today: A proud American speaking out for human rights and democracy, the rule of law, and, as a U.S. Congresswoman, the safety and security of Americans. It is also why I know the costs of freedom and stand firm against Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth’s illegal war.

As a public figure, I fully expect public criticism and wholly respect Americans' constitutional First Amendment rights to free speech. I understand the high emotions during such a tenuous time for those who have family in both Iran and the United States. But I will not tolerate direct threats levied against my loved ones and staff who did not sign up for the public spotlight. I also won’t be silent as they are targeted, doxxed, and attacked online. This has not been a good-faith policy debate. It is a coordinated effort to smear, intimidate, and silence, and it will not succeed.
 
My duty is clear: to uphold the Constitution of the United States and to faithfully serve the people of Arizona’s 3rd Congressional District. It is the honor of my life to represent the people of Arizona in Congress, over 75 percent of whom are deeply opposed to this war. I remain committed to doing so with integrity and transparency.

Today, with the announcement that the first two Arctic Security Cutters will be homeported in Alaska, it is becoming real. This news marks a turning point in America’s investment in the Arctic and will allow us to reassert our influence in the region—enhancing maritime commerce, strengthening cooperation with our allies, increasing deterrence against our adversaries, and ensuring our military can respond to emergencies in any environment. 

I want to commend President Donald Trump for his commitment to these critical assets. When he came into office in 2016, one of my first conversations with him focused on the importance of investing in our infrastructure so we could compete in the Arctic in the 21st century. He listened and came through on his commitment to expanding our icebreaker capacity, and I appreciate his continued dedication to this issue. 

The work is just beginning. As we move to designate Alaska’s new homeport locations, ensuring these ASCs are ready to serve will require significant shoreside infrastructure with new housing to support both the vessels and the influx of personnel. While there is a long road ahead, this announcement means new investment, new jobs, and new opportunities flowing into our communities. Today is a good day for America, a good day for the Arctic, and a good day for Alaska.

“As the son of immigrants from India, I take great pride in my heritage..The comments shared by President Trump are offensive, ignorant and beneath the dignity of the office he holds”

As the son of immigrants from India, I take great pride in both my heritage and in the country that gave my family the opportunity to build a better life. My parents came to the United States legally in search of that opportunity. 

My mother spent 35 years working as a public school teacher. My father worked as an engineer. They instilled in my brothers and me a deep belief in hard work, public service, and giving back to the country that welcomed them.

I am a product of that American story. I attended California’s public schools from kindergarten through medical school, became a doctor, and now have the privilege of serving our nation in Congress. That is what the American Dream looks like.

The comments shared by President Trump are offensive, ignorant, and beneath the dignity of the office he holds. They reflect a fundamental misunderstanding of who we are as a nation. America has always been strengthened by generations of immigrants who come here, work hard, and contribute to our country. They do not weaken America — they strengthen it.

America was built by people from all over the world who believed in its promise and worked tirelessly to make it better for the next generation. That’s the story of my family, and it’s the story of millions of families across our nation.

President Trump, who was born into wealth and privilege, has never had to struggle the way so many immigrant families have. He does not understand the grit, sacrifice, and determination it takes to build a life from the ground up. He does not understand public service, and he does not understand the values that make America the greatest nation in the world.

We are a nation of immigrants, and we are stronger because of it.

Putin is not only trying to seize Ukrainian land. He is trying to erase Ukrainian identity—targeting churches, synagogues, mosques, clergy, and faith communities across Ukraine.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, more than 600 religious sites have been damaged or destroyed, and more than 50 Ukrainian clergy members have been killed. In Russian-occupied territories, religious communities that refuse to submit to Kremlin control have faced raids, detention, forced re-registration, criminal prosecution, and systematic intimidation.

These are not isolated abuses. They are part of a deliberate campaign of repression, and demand a response.

Today, I introduced the Countering Russia’s War on Faith Act to ensure Russia’s persecution of religious communities in Ukraine and Russian-occupied territories is fully documented, exposed, and met with real consequences. My legislation requires the Departments of State and Defense to jointly report on these abuses and identify those responsible for sanctionable actions.

The American Coalition for Ukraine has been a critical partner in this effort, including PA-1 constituent advocates Lauren Henasey, Ihor Chernik, and Olga Mykhaylyuk. We met this week to continue our work together on confronting this persecution directly and ensuring Russia’s assault on religious freedom does not go unanswered. Their insight and advocacy strengthen this effort and help keep the voices of the Ukrainian people at the center of our response.

Together, we will keep standing with Ukraine, defending religious freedom, and holding Russia accountable.

S001203.text:
The irony of posting about Earth Day just a week after we lost a vote to save the Boundary Waters isn’t lost on me. It’s a tough loss that we’re still processing. But today, of all days, should remind us why these special places are worth fighting for.
 
The Boundary Waters have some of the cleanest water that you will find anywhere in this country. Endless lakes and streams filled with bass and pike and trout. Completely untouched nature and only accessible via canoe.

Allowing this copper-sulfide mine in the headwaters of the BWCA will threaten all of that, but the fight isn’t over. It looks different, yes, but the mission is still fundamentally the same: These waters are the birthright of every single one of us, and it’s our job to protect them from the corporate greed of Antofagasta. Not this mine. Not this place.
 
This coalition of Tribal Nations, outdoorsmen, conservationists, public lands enthusiasts and just your average Minnesotans who have been lucky enough to visit this place will still fight against this mine.

And anyone who is feeling defeated should look at the comments on Pete Stauber’s posts last week to get a sense of just how mad we are and how hard we are going to continue fighting.

Because the Boundary Waters have such special meaning. It’s a sacred place, and we will never stop defending it.

INTRODUCING: The Restoring Law and Order on America's Streets Act.

This legislation expands the DOJ's civil commitment authority and restores public order. 

Under current law, the DOJ can seek civil commitment for sexually dangerous people. Our bill expands this authority to include any person who poses a danger to public safety.

A danger to public safety means anyone with a serious mental illness or disorder making it seriously difficult to refrain from:

❌ Violent crime
❌ Burglary, robbery, or larceny
❌ Illegal narcotics distribution in public spaces
❌ Urban camping or squatting
❌ Vandalism

RT by @RepMaxwellFrost: I fully condemn the hateful rhetoric, lies, cruel and deliberate misinformation, and threats that my family, my staff, and I have been subjected to since the Iran War began nearly 8 weeks ago. These coordinated attacks and threats have only continued to worsen, most recently after I introduced Articles of Impeachment against Pete Hegseth. This conduct has crossed the line into threats to our physical safety, which we have reported to law enforcement.

Bad actors have tried to smear my family and staff by circulating fake and AI-generated images and flat-out lying that my parents and I are not U.S. citizens. They have pushed xenophobic and sexist attacks and amplified absurd conspiracy theories about my family. They’ve even gone so far as to spread the outright lie that I am somehow tied to the regime. I will say this once and move on: these absurd allegations are entirely false and I denounce them in the strongest terms.

These attacks aren’t about truth; they’re the product of desperation from those trying to distract from a failing, illegal war, rising costs of living, and an administration with no coherent strategy while Americans pay the price at the pump. And while they spread lies, American service members are being put in harm’s way, with real casualties mounting in a war that lacks both justification and direction.

Let me reiterate, once again, that I have been unequivocal in my opposition to the brutal Islamic Republic regime, its repression of women, and its support for terrorism. My record on this issue is longstanding and crystal clear. My family has personally experienced the regime’s brutality. 

It is in part why I am who I am today: A proud American speaking out for human rights and democracy, the rule of law, and, as a U.S. Congresswoman, the safety and security of Americans. It is also why I know the costs of freedom and stand firm against Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth’s illegal war.

As a public figure, I fully expect public criticism and wholly respect Americans' constitutional First Amendment rights to free speech. I understand the high emotions during such a tenuous time for those who have family in both Iran and the United States. But I will not tolerate direct threats levied against my loved ones and staff who did not sign up for the public spotlight. I also won’t be silent as they are targeted, doxxed, and attacked online. This has not been a good-faith policy debate. It is a coordinated effort to smear, intimidate, and silence, and it will not succeed.
 
My duty is clear: to uphold the Constitution of the United States and to faithfully serve the people of Arizona’s 3rd Congressional District. It is the honor of my life to represent the people of Arizona in Congress, over 75 percent of whom are deeply opposed to this war. I remain committed to doing so with integrity and transparency.

Our TSA officers, Coast Guard service members, and FEMA responders show up every single day to keep Americans safe — the least we can do is make sure they get paid. That's why yesterday I signed a discharge petition to force a vote on funding for these critical DHS agencies. 

These aren't abstract budget numbers. These are real people doing critical, life-saving work for our communities — and they shouldn't have to wonder whether their next paycheck is coming. Restoring their funding is exactly what I was sent here to do, and I'm not letting up until we get it done.

The President just told Americans to accept higher gas prices "for a little while... until the war ends." A war he started with no exit strategy, no congressional authorization, and no plan.
 
Working families don't have a "little while”,  they're paying bills today. This is unacceptable.

This morning, the United States, in coordination with Israel, launched strikes against Iran — a significant military action with serious consequences for our national security.

While I understand the gravity of the threat, the process here cannot be ignored. The War Powers Act exists for a reason: to ensure that no single person can commit this nation to war without accountability to the American people.

When a president bypasses our constitutional process, he isn't just cutting corners — he is undermining the framework that governs this country. This choice has consequences, and Congress must respond accordingly.

For my full press release, visit http://fields.house.gov/media.

Pinned: 🚨Senate Republicans just passed the Secure America Act!

Here’s how we got here:

Back in February, Senate Democrats gave Republicans a choice in order to fund DHS:

1. Prohibit immigration enforcement in the interior of the country, which would essentially end all deportations, (it was absolutely never about so called reforms), or

2. Fund DHS without Border Patrol or ICE, pass that bill, and then fund those agencies through an arcane process that allows us to do it without Democrat votes (what I refer to as the Secure America Act).

We chose #2, and knowing the Senate Democrats will put us in the same situation at the end of this year, we funded Border Patrol and ICE for the next three years.

I am confident that the House will now pass the two bills we sent them and FULLY FUND ALL OF DHS, with Border Patrol and ICE funded through 2029!

Two more points:

Senate Democrats have proven they care more about the welfare of illegals than Americans. Secondly, they used the suffering of 260,000 hard working DHS workers to attempt to hold Republicans hostage.

We did not and will never waiver on our support of law enforcement!

H001100.text:
On my way to the House floor, I had the chance to connect with Trustees from the Town of Silt, including Mayor Pro-Tem Derek Hanrahan and Town Manager Jim Mann.

We had a detailed conversation about infrastructure priorities in Silt, such as the planned non-motorized pedestrian bridge over Interstate-70 that will improve safety and connectivity for residents moving between parts of the community. We also discussed the broader role federal support can play in helping small towns move projects like this forward, along with the importance of protecting Shoshone water rights — which are critical to maintaining consistent flows through Glenwood Canyon and supporting agriculture, recreation, and local economies across the Western Slope.

These are the kinds of conversations that shape how I approach the work in Washington, grounded in real projects, real needs, and making sure communities like Silt have a strong voice in the decisions that affect them. #CO03 #GarfieldCounty

One step closer to delivering reliable water solutions for Southwest Colorado.

Yesterday, H.R. 5911, the Crystal Reservoir Conveyance Act, passed through the House Natural Resources Committee. This legislation transfers Crystal Reservoir to the City of Ouray, giving local leaders the ability to repair critical infrastructure, restore water access, and better support agriculture, wildfire response, and recreation across the region.

Water is foundational to communities across #CO03. This is a practical step to put decision-making back in local hands, reduce federal barriers, and ensure this resource is managed by the people who depend on it every day.

Appreciate the support of Chairman Westerman to advance this bill. We’ll keep pushing to get it across the finish line. #OurayCounty

Spent time this weekend in Mesa County with Club 20 sharing what I’ve learned so far in Congress—and how those new experiences now shape the way I approach this job.

One thing has become clear: the best policy comes from listening to the people back home and staying focused on practical solutions that actually work in rural communities. That means cutting through the noise in Washington and making sure the priorities of Western and Southern Colorado are what drive decisions.

I also talked through the Community Project Funding I’ve secured for #CO03 this year. In total, we delivered over $11 million for projects across Colorado’s Third District, with $3.19 million going directly to projects in Mesa County.

Those investments include funding for infrastructure improvements, water systems, and public safety projects that support continued growth in Grand Junction and the surrounding communities.

This is what effective representation looks like, bringing federal resources back home in a way that strengthens local communities and supports long-term growth across the district. #MesaCounty

Met with leaders from the Colorado Association of School Executives, including Alamosa Superintendent Diana Jones, to hear directly what schools are facing across the state.

The message was consistent. School leaders are dealing with tight budgets, workforce shortages, and the challenge of attracting and retaining teachers, especially in rural communities.

Strong schools are at the center of every community, but they cannot succeed without stable funding and a workforce pipeline that reflects the realities on the ground. My focus is making sure federal policy supports those needs and keeps opportunities within reach for families across #CO03.

Last week I traveled to the Southern Ute Reservation in Ignacio to join Coloradans from across the state in honoring the life of Senator Ben Nighthorse Campbell.  Senator Campbell represented Colorado’s Third District in the House before serving in the U.S. Senate. A decorated veteran and a member of the Northern Cheyenne Tribe, he brought an independent voice to Congress and became a leading advocate for Native American communities nationwide.  He approached public service with a clear sense of duty and a willingness to stand apart when it mattered. His focus was always on the people he represented, not the politics of the moment.  I will keep his wife, Linda, and their family in my thoughts and prayers. #CO03

WORLD_FRANCE_PRESIDENT.text:
Pleased to meet with President @ZelenskyUA again on the sidelines of the informal European Council in Cyprus.
                   
I welcome the release of the European loan for Ukraine, which sends a very strong signal of our determination to continue standing by Ukraine’s side. The agreement reached on the 20th package of sanctions is also a clear message to Russia.

We held a comprehensive discussion on our defence cooperation, on the need to further increase pressure on Russia’s war economy, and on the work we are carrying out as part of the Coalition of the Willing.

Our support will not weaken, either today or tomorrow. Europe keeps its promises, and it will stand firm.

Heureux de retrouver le Président @ZelenskyUA en marge du Conseil européen informel à Chypre.
                       
Je salue le déblocage du prêt européen pour l’Ukraine, qui constitue un signal très fort de notre détermination à continuer de nous tenir aux côtés de l’Ukraine. L'accord obtenu sur le 20ème paquet de sanctions est également un message clair adressé à la Russie.

Nous avons fait un point complet sur notre coopération de défense, sur la nécessité de renforcer encore la pression sur l’économie de guerre de la Russie et sur le travail que nous effectuons dans le cadre de la Coalition des Volontaires.

Notre soutien ne faiblira ni aujourd’hui, ni demain. L’Europe tient parole, elle tiendra bon.
Aux jeunes : ayez le goût de l’avenir !
